B_Neuroscienze.text:
The potentiating phenomenon of long-term potentiation (LTP) mediated by N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors is a fundamental mechanism underlying learning and memory consolidation in the brain. At the molecular level, LTP is characterized by a persistent increase in the strength of synaptic transmission between neurons, which is thought to be mediated by the activation of NMDA receptors.
